title: Provisioning negotiation broker for Dedicated capacity requests and approvals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Reservation requests for Dedicated capacity are currently handled via ad-hoc form submissions and manual spreadsheets. This causes slow approval cycles, inconsistent SLA commitments, and friction when negotiating throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior. Operators spend significant time matching requests to available fleet capacity and translating business-level throughput commitments into specific pool and autoscale configurations.
Goals: 1) Provide a deterministic, auditable provisioning negotiation broker that turns customer reservation requests into approved capacity allocations and config artifacts. 2) Surface automated feasibility checks (capacity, region, cost), negotiated SLO/throughput commitments, and recommended autoscaling policies. 3) Integrate approvals with RBAC, audit logs, billing quotes, and capacity planning forecasts so that engineering and sales can move faster and with fewer errors.
Scope: - New "Provisioning Negotiation Broker" service (UI + API + workflows) to intake requests, run feasibility, propose configurations, and automate approval handoffs. - Approval templates for common reservation types (steady throughput, bursty workloads, strict latency SLOs). - Automated cost estimate and billing quote generation integrated with pricing engine. - Hooks for operators to adjust pool assignment and autoscale policy before final approval. - Audit trail and notifications (Slack/Email/Confluence links) for every decision. Out of scope for initial launch: fully automated legal SLA contract generation and exports to external contract systems. Those will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Request template available for customers and internal AE to create new Dedicated reservation requests (fields: requested throughput RPS, p95 latency target, preferred region, start/end dates, expected token volumes).
Broker runs automated feasibility check against current fleet inventory and returns recommended pool(s), expected provisioning lead time, and cost estimate within 90 seconds for 90% of requests.
Approval flow supports: auto-approve for low-risk templates, manual operator approval for medium/high risk, and escalations to finance/legal for custom SLA terms.

Approved reservation results in: a) an assigned capacity bucket in the capacity planner, b) a provisioning ticket in ENG with prefilled config (pool id, node type, reserved vCPU/GPU), and c) billing quote recorded in billing system.
Audit log entries created for each state transition (requested -> feasibility -> proposed -> approved -> provisioned) and surfaced in Console activity feed.
End-to-end test showing that a pilot customer can submit a request and receive final provisioned capacity within the SLA lead time defined in the acceptance test.
Security review completed and signoff recorded prior to beta rollout.
design_notes: Broker will call Capacity Forecast API (ENG-21234) for current and projected inventory and will call Pricing Engine (PM-14200) for cost estimates.
Feasibility engine heuristics: match region and hardware type, consider reserved pools and burst capacity, simulate autoscaling policy impact (min/max nodes, warm pool).
Autoscale policy recommendations: presets for 'steady', 'bursty', 'latency-sensitive' with suggested min/max and scale step sizes. Presets editable by operators.
Approval UI: inline compare of 'requested throughput' vs 'guaranteed throughput' with visual risk indicator and cost delta. Include 'fast-track' toggle for AE approved low-risk requests.
Authorization: use existing SSO/RBAC roles. Only users with 'Capacity Operator' role can approve medium/high risk reservations.
Telemetry: instrument events for request created, feasibility completed, proposal accepted/rejected, provisioned. Tag events with customer id and request id.
Data retention: audit trail retained per compliance policy (90 days for trial, 7 years for enterprise contracts).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot, 2 weeks): Internal pilot with AE + Solutions Eng on two customers (one steady throughput, one bursty). Monitor time-to-approve and provisioning errors.
Phase 2 (beta, 4 weeks): Open to selected public customers; enable auto-approve for 'low-risk' templates and manual flow for others. Collect operator feedback and iterate UX.
Phase 3 (GA): Turn on full integration with billing quotes and capacity planner; provide migration tool for existing reservations; publish runbook.
Rollback plan: If provisioning failures > 2% or SLA lead time regresses, disable auto-provisioning and revert to manual ticket creation until hotfix deployed.
metrics: Median time from request submission to approval (target: < 24h for manual, < 1h for auto-approve).
Provisioning success rate on first attempt (target: >= 98%).
Forecast accuracy: % of approved reserved capacity that matches actual usage after first 30 days (target: 75%+).
Number of SLA disputes opened within 90 days of provisioning (target: < 2%).
Operator time saved (estimated hours/month) compared to manual spreadsheet workflow.
